headline: US power utilities are tightening the rules for new data center customers, demanding financial guarantees to screen out 'phantom' projects that ask for grid power they may never use.
score_reason: Fresh, specific numbers from a leading paper and a utility; no sign of overstatement, but read through a relay.
importance_line: Households that could otherwise end up sharing the cost of grid upgrades for data centers that never open are better protected, developers face higher upfront costs, and the 23 percent figure is one research firm's estimate, not a count of cancelled projects.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that grid-connection requests from AI data centers are swamping utilities and many will never be built; Wood Mackenzie, a research firm, puts only 23 percent of disclosed requests in its 'high confidence' category. Exelon, a utility serving the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, says demanding binding financial commitments cut its high-probability list from 18,000 to 11,000 megawatts, and Texas now requires a $50,000-per-megawatt deposit before engineering studies.
notes: WSJ original is login-walled (HTTP 401); read Breitbart News's summary of the WSJ report and used only the WSJ-attributed parts.
